It seems the typical Iowa family farmer is over 60 years old, female, and has children that have chosen to take up a different profession. Farms that have been in the family for three or more generations are being sold to consortiums that will combine them with nearby or adjacent farms to form a new "food factory", or are bought by speculators that will develop the land into, for example, housing developments.

The family farm cannot afford to hire the people or buy the machinery and technology to compete with the "big boys" in terms of yield per acre. Most Iowa family farms nowadays are not being handed down, but rather are being put up for auction when the farmer retires, if the land is not purchased by an adjacent landowner.
